verdict.root_cause: A platform-automation traffic-shaping container was attached to cartservice's network namespace at 06:10:51, about three minutes before onset, applying a fixed 300ms egress delay with zero jitter, and it was still in place at onset [tr_87d8cba14dd3]. Traces show exactly that shape: every cartservice Redis egress span (HGET and HMSET) sits at a uniform ~300-305ms floor with negligible cartservice self time, so GetCart costs ~302ms and AddItem ~602-611ms as the penalty scales with Redis round trips [tr_8674b22837af]. The wait is inherited upward into frontend (~605-918ms cart spans, ~1510ms HTTP POSTs) while all non-cart dependencies stay at baseline [tr_8674b22837af]. cartservice itself is healthy - clean startup, successful Redis connect, continuous served cart operations [tr_1a7afb458acd] - and checkoutservice completes orders with no error lines [tr_1283b292d744]. The mechanism is waiting on an artificially slowed egress path, not a crash, bad artifact, or resource exhaustion.
verdict.reasoning: The change record and the traces agree independently on both magnitude and shape: a declared 300ms/0-jitter injection [tr_87d8cba14dd3] and an observed uniform ~300-305ms additive floor confined to cartservice's Redis hop [tr_8674b22837af]. Zero dispersion excludes queueing or load saturation; unaffected sibling dependencies in the same traces exclude a node-wide or mesh-wide fault [tr_8674b22837af]. Frontend and checkoutservice alerted as callers - their span durations decompose into cartservice children, and both otherwise serve normally [tr_8674b22837af, tr_1a7afb458acd, tr_1283b292d744]. The rival change candidates are dead: the hotfix image was reverted ~13 min before onset and the REDIS_ADDR:6380 edit ~3.3h before [tr_87d8cba14dd3]. This is dependency_latency rather than bad_config because the injected value is not a wrong address or limit - it inserts delay into a call path, and the waiting is the failure. The fix is removing the shaping container, a config_revert, not an artifact rollback.
open_questions: Frontend's only error-ratio change point is at 05:53 [tr_5d2555a4698f], ~18 minutes before the 06:10:51 attach [tr_87d8cba14dd3]; the injection cannot explain error elevation that predates it, and this gap was never resolved.

cartservice has no metric series at all - error ratio empty across incident and baseline for 4+ hours [tr_268b615acad8, tr_0108add572a4] - so rate, latency, restarts and readiness remain unmeasured, and the trace sample carries no timestamps to pin onset [tr_8674b22837af].

Checkout's ~900ms unaccounted time above cartservice children [tr_8674b22837af], and whether the sidecar is still attached now (no removal record, yet flows looked clean by 06:15:32 [tr_1283b292d744, tr_1a7afb458acd]).

alternatives.root_cause: A separate unidentified fault starting ~05:53 drives frontend's error step, with the cart latency injection a concurrent but distinct condition.
alternatives.why_not: The frontend metric has no downstream-target dimension and no latency series, so it attributes nothing [tr_5d2555a4698f], while traces positively locate the inflation below cartservice [tr_8674b22837af]. It survives only on the unresolved 05:53 timing conflict.

alternatives.root_cause: Redis (redis-cart) itself became slow, and cartservice is faithfully reporting a genuinely degraded backend.
alternatives.why_not: A real backend slowdown would show dispersion; the observed latency is a near-constant zero-variance floor matching the declared 300ms shaping parameter exactly, and the shaping is applied on cartservice's own eth0 rather than at Redis [tr_87d8cba14dd3, tr_8674b22837af].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating cartservice with its pre-injection configuration should drop the traffic-shaping attachment on its network namespace. Observable in Jaeger: Redis egress spans (HGET/HMSET) falling off the uniform ~300-305ms floor to low single-digit ms, GetCart from ~302ms and AddItem from ~602-611ms to near-baseline, and frontend HTTP POST spans from ~1510-1528ms back toward baseline. cartservice has no metric series at all, so traces and checkoutservice log stage gaps are the only usable confirmation.
proposal.if_wrong: Redis egress spans still sit at a ~300ms floor after the recreate - meaning the shaping lives outside cartservice's own config (host qdisc, platform-automation re-attaching on its repeating schedule) and this action does not reach it. Also falsifying: frontend's error ratio stays elevated, which it likely will, since its only change point is 05:53, ~18 minutes before the 06:10:51 attach - that elevation has a separate, unexplained cause this proposal does not address.
proposal.risk: If the delay is not sourced from cartservice's recorded configuration, this recreates a healthy container for nothing: cart in-memory state is discarded, in-flight cart and checkout calls fail during the restart, and we have burned a change without touching the mechanism. Worse, the change history shows five image flips and two REDIS_ADDR edits in this window; reverting to an ill-chosen prior config could restore the wrong Redis address (port 6380) and break cart persistence outright.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice's callers see connection resets for the duration of the recreate: frontend (GetCart/AddItem) and checkoutservice (GetCart/EmptyCart), and through them loadgenerator traffic. checkoutservice order flows may fail mid-placement during the window.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerted near-simultaneously across the cart/checkout/frontend path, which is more than a single isolated warning and cannot be dismissed. Cart appearing first with fan-out through checkout suggests a shared downstream dependency slowdown.
